title: Does Frontier AI Strengthen Cyber Defense? Evidence from Project Glasswing
abstract: arXiv:2611.06629v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Defenders and attackers race to find the same software flaws. I use the launch of Project Glasswing, which gave a small group of large US tech firms early access to Claude Mythos Preview, a model for finding software vulnerabilities, to study how access to frontier AI affects defenders, external researchers, and attackers. Using the universe of publicly disclosed vulnerabilities, I find that firms with access more than doubled their disclosures relative to Chinese and Russian tech firms without access, disclosed about 150 percent more high-impact vulnerabilities, and fixed reported flaws as quickly as before. As treated firms found more flaws themselves, external researchers, who sell their findings through bug bounties, reported about half as many vulnerabilities in treated firms' code and more in other firms' code, without leaving the market. translated_title: 前沿AI能否增强网络防御？来自“玻璃翼项目”的证据
translated_abstract: 防御者与攻击者竞相寻找相同的软件缺陷。本文利用“玻璃翼项目”的启动来研究获取前沿AI如何影响防御者、外部研究者和攻击者——该项目让一小部分美国大型科技公司提前获得了Claude Mythos Preview，一种用于发现软件漏洞的模型。基于公开披露的全部漏洞数据，我发现获得访问权限的公司相对于没有访问权限的中国和俄罗斯科技公司，其漏洞披露数量增加了一倍以上，披露的高影响漏洞多出约150%，且修复已报告缺陷的速度与以前一样快。由于受影响的公司自己发现了更多缺陷，通过漏洞赏金出售研究结果的外部研究者在受影响公司代码中报告的漏洞减少了约一半，而在其他公司代码中报告的漏洞增多，且并未退出市场。没有证据表明攻击者利用了这些额外的漏洞：被利用的份额（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文利用“玻璃翼项目”作为准自然实验，发现前沿AI漏洞发现模型使获得访问权限的美国科技公司漏洞披露翻倍、高影响漏洞披露增加约150%，外部赏金研究者将报告转向其他公司，且未见攻击者利用额外漏洞的证据，表明前沿AI目前主要强化了网络防御而非攻击。
en_tdlr: Using the launch of Project Glasswing as a quasi-natural experiment, this paper finds that frontier AI vulnerability-finding models more than doubled disclosure of vulnerabilities and raised high-impact disclosures by about 150 percent among treated US tech firms, shifted external bug-bounty researchers' reports toward other firms, and showed no evidence of increased attacker exploitation, suggesting frontier AI currently strengthens cyber defense.
